messages:
olivia (eng-security): heads up — npm audit bubbled up 3 high/1 critical vuln in console/ui deps during CI tonight. main offenders: serialize-javascript, ws, and dot-prop. full list in the audit output attached to the CI run.

kevin (frontend): ugh. which ones need immediate patching vs acceptable to defer? any of these transitive through build tooling?

olivia (eng-security): serialize-javascript -> direct dep via react-scripts (dev dep), ws -> direct in live-reload layer, dot-prop -> transitive via css-loader. summary:
- CVE-2025-serial: serialize-javascript (high) — attacker can inject via crafted input in SSR path (console uses a small SSR dev util)
- CVE-2025-ws: ws (high) — causes DoS in watcher in dev, not exposed to prod build but our Dedicated demo runs it in staging
- CVE-2024-dotprop: dot-prop (critical) — prototype pollution in a transitive chain used by webpack config loader (affects build step)

sam (devex): lockfile churn is going to be real if we bump wide. can we target minimal fixes? i.e., pin vulnerable packages to patched ranges and run `npm ci` then `pnpm import`? also we should avoid changing major tool versions right now to keep predictable CI.

kevin (frontend): plan: 1) patch dot-prop in the build step first (blocks CI), 2) patch serialize-javascript in dev SSR util (low blast to prod), 3) ws in staging-only. i'll open a single PR with scoped package updates + a note about focusing on the lockfile diff. will run full e2e and local build.

natalie (secops): make sure the PR includes: commit message referencing CVE ids, impact assessment (prod vs dev/staging), and a checklist for release artifacts to be signed. we need audit log entries for who approved and merged. if dot-prop fix affects build outputs, we should produce a deterministic build artifact and record SLSA metadata.

olivia (eng-security): agreed. add the following triage priorities:
- P0: dot-prop (critical, breaks CI/build produce arbitrary code path) — ship within 24h to CI + block merges until green
- P1: serialize-javascript (high, limited to dev SSR) — ship within 72h, verify no prod bundles change
- P2: ws (high, staging only) — schedule during next maintenance window if no exploit path to prod

kevin (frontend): i'll include a `package.json` snippet in the PR:
```
"resolutions": {
  "dot-prop": "^5.3.1",
  "serialize-javascript": "^5.0.1"
}
```
Will that be acceptable or do we want to update the root lockfile only?

sam (devex): resolutions are fine for a short-term stopgap but they cause lockfile churn across workspaces. prefer patching the direct dependents (webpack/css-loader) to pick up patched transitive deps if possible. if we must use `resolutions`, add an explicit comment and remove it after upstreams cut releases. Also update our shrinkwrap/lockfile policy doc for this incident.

audit-bot: automated-audit-report: npm-audit-run #1768904321 -> 3 vulnerabilities (1 critical, 2 high). Suggested fixes: update css-loader, webpack (minor), and serialize-javascript. CI run: https://ci.internal/runs/1768904321 (logs attached).

natalie (secops): we also need to think about release process for Redwood Dedicated customers. if this change touches build tooling that customers run (private deployments), we must coordinate with account teams and set expectations. cc @kevin

kevin (frontend): noted. tagging customer-impact label in PR and will draft an email template for customer success if Dedicated packages need a rebuild.

olivia (eng-security): final asks for PR: change log entry, CVE ids, short risk blurb, test plan (build+e2e), and rollback instructions (revert PR + pin old lockfile snapshot). i'll schedule a quick 30-min review slot after you open it.

kevin (frontend): will open PR in ~1h with minimal resolution changes, run full CI, and add the requested metadata. thanks. :thumbsup:

sam (devex): FYI i'll run a canary deploy of the console package to staging once CI is green to validate assets and check bundle hashes. i'll also capture lockfile diff size and paste it into the PR to help reviewers focus on relevant entries.

olivia (eng-security): awesome — please @mention me when it's ready. thanks team.
